title: jack-ketch project config (v3)
description: Project config for jack-ketch v3. Served by ConfigService.GetSchema and used by editors via yaml-language-server.

runtime.description: Daemon runtime defaults for this project.

stop_grace.description: Grace period before SIGKILL after SIGTERM.

log_buffer_lines.description: Ring buffer lines retained per process.

max_exited_processes.description: How many exited processes to keep listed.

exited_ttl.description: How long to keep exited processes listed before auto-removal.

mode.description: Trusted is the default permissive posture; restricted confines commands and workdirs.

apps.description: Named apps that can be started with Start or StartStack.

type.description: Process type or profile, e.g. node, python, shell.

workdir.description: Working directory, relative to the workspace root.

env_file.description: Dotenv file applied to this app, relative to project root.

env.description: Environment entries as KEY=VALUE; supports ${port:name} templates.

readiness.description: Regex patterns that mark the app ready when matched in logs.

http.description: HTTP URL to probe for health.

tcp.description: TCP address to probe for health.

max_restarts.description: Max restarts within the backoff window.

lifetime.description: Persistent survives session close; session stops after lease grace.

autostart.description: Start automatically when the workspace loads.

reload.description: Manual marks stale on config change; restart restarts automatically.

pty.description: Allocate a PTY for colors and interactive CLIs.

depends_on.description: Other apps that must start first; used by StartStack order.

ports.description: Named ports for templating and conflict detection.

redact.description: Regex patterns; matches are replaced with *** in GetLogs/Search/Tail output.

alerts.description: Notify (event + GUI toast) when a pattern appears in any process's logs.

pattern.description: Substring or regex (see regex) to match against each log line.

regex.description: Treat pattern as a regular expression instead of a plain substring.
